materialization.note: Re-keyed 2026-09-20 from the captured full item record. It was `item/local:<slug>` with `parents: []` -- an item this repository held and could not place -- because no record had been captured for it. One has, so the id is now the DSpace UUID from the captured page's own URL, the parents are the breadcrumb, and the bitstream's `of` is the Handle rather than a `local:` origin. The slug survives as `libraryId`, which is what the ingested text is filed under and what every existing reference resolves through.

materialization.note: DERIVED HERE, and not the THUMBNAIL bundle IRIS generates. These bytes were rendered here from page 1 of 9789241548960_eng.pdf by cat-harness/scripts/pdf-cover.py (pymupdf 1.28.2) on 2026-09-20, scaled to 300px wide from a 453.54x680.32pt page; the height follows the page's own aspect and is never forced. iris.who.int is egress-blocked from this environment (CONNECT 403, bean r1lz), so no upstream thumbnail was fetched or compared. `of` therefore names the local PDF this was made from rather than a WHO URI: the Handle identifies the ITEM, and asserting it here would say IRIS supplied this image. Page 1 is taken as the cover because page 1 is a determined answer and "the cover" is not -- the same choice pdf-pages.py makes about sections. Verified by `bun run who-iris/scripts/gen-covers.ts --check`, which re-renders and compares these bytes, this digest and these dimensions.
IDENTIFIERS UNKNOWN, as above. The slug is an ISBN, which is a real identifier but not IRIS's -- it names the publication, not the repository item, and the two are not interchangeable for resolution.
